summary: Port color-major bucket construction and dispatch sizing as an ordered native program.
regressions: 56 cases cover empty and partial workgroups, histogram-eligible Rust fixtures, generic strided loops, multiple batches and bucket scans over multiple blocks
Inactive slots with stale body IDs, zero/MAX/out-of-range colors, copied link bits and inverse-index permutations
Statistics cover colors above 63, exclude unsolved contacts, preserve unused buffers, and clamp synthetic large dispatches at 256 groups
Both legal atomic permutations and corruption rejection are checked; original Rust histogram shaders execute through the cooperative CPU oracle
differences: Count/scatter use Rust generic global atomics on every target; the single-batch shared-memory histogram optimization is explicitly deferred. This changes allocation order and cost, not bucket membership or copied link bits.
The ordered program follows the original reset/count/scan/scatter/dispatch sequence with no host physics/readback between kernels.
No floating point arithmetic or tolerance changes. Full frame scheduling and Ascend hardware execution remain unvalidated.
Reuse the existing cooperative Rust prefix helper for bucket fixtures without changing its arithmetic.
